findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite an inspection (Read/grep) of the PINNED pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py confirming the exact dispatch attribute AnthropicModel uses for real requests (that it is self.client.beta.messages.create, and whether it is called live vs bound once at construction), so the late-binding wrapper is proven on the real request path.
evidence: Plan: 'Pydantic-ai's AnthropicModel._messages_create dispatches every real request through self.client.beta.messages.create(...), so late-binding that instance method is on the real request path.'
resolve_symbol('_messages_create', 'pydantic_ai.models.anthropic') => UNRESOLVED (private method; not proof of absence, and not confirmation of the dispatch-attribute string)
The pydantic_ai source under .venv is not readable by the repo-scoped file tools, so the exact dispatch attribute could not be inspected in this review.
findings.finding: The load-bearing claim that pydantic-ai's AnthropicModel._messages_create dispatches every real request through self.client.beta.messages.create(...) — on which the entire late-binding wrapper strategy depends — is asserted from knowledge of the installed pydantic-ai, but the plan does not cite a Read/inspection of the pinned pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py confirming this dispatch site (and its exact call attribute, e.g. beta.messages.create vs messages.create).
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan', 5th bullet ('Handle Anthropic 1.x beta messages.create signature removal…')
scenarios: If pinned pydantic-ai routes create through a different attribute (e.g. self.client.messages.create, or a helper that binds the method reference at import) the wrapper late-bound onto beta.messages.create is never invoked and unsupported sampling kwargs reach the 1.x SDK signature, re-raising the removed-kwarg error on the real request path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an evidence line quoting the pinned pydantic_ai AnthropicModel source showing the beta.messages.create call site, and have the test_transport_retry.py httpx2 case assert the wrapper is actually reached (e.g. that a relocated temperature reaches extra_body) rather than merely constructing the model.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a construction-time (or test-time) guard asserting the late-bound beta.messages.create wrapper is actually on AnthropicModel's dispatch path (e.g. assert the wrapped instance method is invoked in the AC's real-request-path test), so a future in-range pydantic-ai refactor of the private _messages_create dispatch fails loudly rather than silently bypassing the wrapper.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Pydantic-ai's AnthropicModel._messages_create dispatches every real request through self.client.beta.messages.create(...), so late-binding that instance method is on the real request path.'
resolve_symbol confirms AnthropicModel EXISTS but its private _messages_create method body / dispatch path is not observable via repo-scoped tools (site-packages outside repo root).
Evidence class: Partially-verified (the class exists; the specific private dispatch surface the wrapper hooks is unconfirmed and unpinned across pydantic-ai>=1.107,<2).
findings.finding: The sampling-kwarg relocation strategy depends on an UNVERIFIED private pydantic-ai contract: that AnthropicModel._messages_create dispatches every request through self.client.beta.messages.create(...). This private method is not verifiable from repo-scoped tools and may vary across the widened pydantic-ai (<2) range, silently breaking the late-bound wrapper if the dispatch path changes.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan', bullet 'Handle Anthropic 1.x beta messages.create signature removal ...'
scenarios: A future in-range pydantic-ai release refactors _messages_create to call self.client.beta.messages.create via a different binding (e.g. a captured reference or a submethod), so the late-bound wrapper is bypassed and unsupported sampling kwargs reach the 1.x SDK signature again -> TypeError at real request time.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/extend an acceptance criterion asserting the wrapper DROPS `anthropic.Omit` sampling placeholders (no extra_body entry) while relocating only real values, verified on the final wire JSON.
evidence: Plan: 'The wrapper moves unsupported real sampling kwargs (temperature, top_p, top_k) into extra_body and only drops anthropic.Omit placeholders.'

AC 4 covers 'sampling-kwarg relocation' and AC 6 covers 'sampling values remain visible' but neither states an Omit-placeholder case is verified (i.e. an omitted sampling kwarg is dropped, NOT relocated as a literal Omit).
findings.finding: The wrapper's described behavior of dropping `anthropic.Omit` placeholders (as distinct from relocating real sampling kwargs into extra_body) has no acceptance criterion that explicitly exercises it.
findings.location: Plan bullet 5 ('only drops anthropic.Omit placeholders') vs AC 4/AC 6
scenarios: A model with no configured temperature passes anthropic.Omit; if the wrapper relocated it into extra_body as an Omit literal instead of dropping it, the wire body would carry a bogus value and no AC would catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC 6 (or add AC) to assert that when a sampling kwarg is `anthropic.Omit`, the normalized wire payload contains no corresponding key, and only real sampling values appear as top-level fields.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting that an absent or ambiguous http_client annotation resolves to the stdlib-httpx branch (the plan's stated default).
evidence: Plan text: 'match annotation text containing httpx2.AsyncClient ... Default to stdlib httpx when the annotation is absent or ambiguous.'
ACs test the 1.2.0 (httpx2) and 0.121.0 (httpx) annotation cases but no AC names a test for an absent/ambiguous annotation resolving to the stdlib default — a new conditional branch left unverified.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new decision branch — 'Default to stdlib httpx when the annotation is absent or ambiguous' — but no acceptance criterion exercises that default/fallback branch. The tests named cover the two concrete annotation cases (httpx2.AsyncClient present -> httpx2; 0.121.0 -> httpx) but not the absent/ambiguous-annotation path that routes to the stdlib default.
findings.location: Plan: 'Detect the SDK contract by reading inspect.signature(...).annotation; ... Default to stdlib httpx when the annotation is absent or ambiguous.' and Acceptance criteria (test list)
scenarios: A future/edge SDK build whose http_client annotation is missing or non-matching silently mis-routes to httpx2 (or errors) with no test guarding the intended stdlib-default fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a case to tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py that stubs an AsyncAnthropic-like signature with no/ambiguous http_client annotation and asserts the seam selects the stdlib httpx module.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `tests/external/test_candidate_tracing_live.py` to the AC-7 transport-patch inventory (it uses the same `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport`->MockTransport seam for a real Anthropic FallbackModel), or state why the external tier is deferred; re-derive the full inventory by grepping for the `AsyncHTTPTransport` monkeypatch string plus a symbol-reference sweep so no direct-Anthropic harness is missed.
evidence: Plan AC-7 lists exactly: test_llm_fallback_chain.py, test_agentic_message_cache.py, test_llm_provider_factory.py, test_llm_timeouts.py, test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py, test_candidate_tracing.py, test_candidate_tracing_oracle.py, test_llm_config_gate_root.py
tests/external/test_candidate_tracing_live.py:73: `monkeypatch.setattr(httpx, "AsyncHTTPTransport", lambda *a, **kw: httpx.MockTransport(_handler))`

Its docstring (line 17): 'a real Anthropic FallbackModel runs against an httpx MockTransport'; line 55-57: 'the same seam the unit oracle uses' — where test_candidate_tracing_oracle.py IS in the plan's list but the live variant is not
findings.finding: The AC-7 direct-Anthropic MockTransport harness inventory omits `tests/external/test_candidate_tracing_live.py`, which patches the stdlib `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` seam for a real Anthropic FallbackModel — the same seam the 8 listed files use. Under the httpx2 branch (anthropic 1.x), patching `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` no longer intercepts requests routed through `httpx2`, so this test breaks or leaks a real request just as the enumerated files would.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'Existing direct-Anthropic MockTransport harnesses are updated to patch the SDK-selected transport module in tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py, ... test_llm_config_gate_root.py.'
scenarios: tests/external/test_candidate_tracing_live.py: under anthropic 1.x the FallbackModel routes through httpx2, but the test still patches stdlib httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport, so the MockTransport is never hit — the test breaks (or leaks a real/blocked request) undetected when REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 + [tracing] extra is present

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime.py and test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py to AC-7's harness inventory (or explicitly state why the beta.messages.create wrapping does not touch their _FakeAsyncAnthropic path), since they drive _build_retrying_anthropic_provider via provider_factory('anthropic') with a fake client lacking `.beta.messages.create`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime.py:39-59 defines `class _FakeAsyncAnthropic` that only records kwargs and sets `self.max_retries`; it is monkeypatched over `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` and has no `.beta.messages.create` attribute.

tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime.py:62-91 call `session.provider_factory('anthropic')`, which routes through ProviderSession._build_anthropic -> _build_retrying_anthropic_provider (providers.py:224).
Plan step: 'wrapping the rebar-owned anthropic_client.beta.messages.create instance after provider construction' — this attribute access runs during builder execution these tests exercise.
Both files (and the _heldout twin at tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py) are absent from the AC-7 enumerated list.
findings.finding: AC-7's direct-Anthropic MockTransport harness inventory omits test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime.py and test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py, which drive the changed _build_retrying_anthropic_provider seam via ProviderSession.provider_factory('anthropic') using a _FakeAsyncAnthropic that lacks `.beta.messages.create`; the plan's new post-construction wrapping of `anthropic_client.beta.messages.create` would break them.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, AC-7 (test-update inventory) vs Plan step 5 (wrap beta.messages.create after provider construction)
scenarios: Running test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime after the seam adds beta.messages.create wrapping: the fake client has no `beta` attribute -> AttributeError before the auth-injection assertions run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the dual-contract detection heuristic and the local httpx2 transport-wrapper stopgap (including the 'prefer first-party HTTPX2TenacityTransport when available' upgrade path) in an ADR or AGENTS.md note.
evidence: Plan: 'the current pinned pydantic-ai lacks it, so this patch uses a local httpx2.AsyncBaseTransport wrapper with the same retry/validate/close/context-manager behavior.'
No plan bullet or AC mentions recording the dual-contract detection / local-wrapper decision in a durable design doc; the rationale currently lives only in this ticket.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new local httpx2 transport-wrapper pattern (`HTTPX2TenacityTransport` fallback) but does not capture this architectural decision or the SDK-contract-detection approach in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.location: Plan bullet 4 (local httpx2.AsyncBaseTransport wrapper) and detection bullet 2
scenarios: A future maintainer upgrading pydantic-ai (which may add first-party HTTPX2TenacityTransport) needs to know the local wrapper was a deliberate stopgap and when to remove it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the `beta.messages.create` wrapper is applied exactly once per freshly-constructed client, cannot double-wrap an already-patched create, and does not depend on eager materialization of the `beta.messages` resource.
evidence: Plan: 'wrapping the rebar-owned anthropic_client.beta.messages.create instance after provider construction' and 'late-binding that instance method is on the real request path'

The current seam builds a fresh client per _build_retrying_anthropic_provider call (anthropic_model.py:214), so wrap application is per-construction; the plan does not state a guard against re-wrapping a client whose create was already patched.
findings.finding: The sampling-kwarg relocation wraps `anthropic_client.beta.messages.create` as a late-bound instance method 'after provider construction', but the plan does not specify the binding's ordering/idempotency guarantees — whether the wrap is applied exactly once, how it behaves if `beta.messages` is lazily materialized by the SDK, and that a re-entrant or double provider build cannot stack wrappers (relocating already-relocated kwargs).
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan', bullet: 'Handle Anthropic 1.x beta messages.create signature removal by wrapping ...'
scenarios: A provider rebuilt within one process, or a create attribute already patched, gets its wrapper applied twice, potentially relocating kwargs into extra_body more than once or shadowing the original bound method.
